tagline: Evidence-bounded merge-trigger engineering for pulsed FRC fusion — causal software, bit-true RTL, and machine-checked safety.
summary: SCPN-MIF-CORE is a pre-alpha research-to-hardware stack for deterministic phase synchronisation and pulsed field-reversed-configuration merge-trigger decisions. It joins Python and Rust kinematic and lifecycle models with Q8.8 SystemVerilog trigger fabrics, local Verilator cosimulation, SymbiYosys properties, and a federated Studio evidence surface. Published evidence establishes software behaviour, bit-true local-simulator parity, and formal clock-cycle relations; named-device post-route timing, calibrated hardware-in-the-loop evidence, full FUSION reference parity, and facility-grade actuation remain explicitly gated.
highlights: Causal streaming and retrospective batch merge-trigger engines expose fire, unsafe-abort, bank-infeasible, and hold outcomes with veto dominance, debounce, arm, and bank-readiness semantics pinned by tests.
Synthesisable MIF-007 sensor quantisation and MIF-008 trigger/fast-veto RTL are paired with open-tool safety, liveness, reachability, and timing-property suites.
Python-versus-Verilator cosimulation is reported as cosim:local-verilator on the simulator substrate, never as FPGA waveform equivalence or hardware-in-the-loop validation.
Measured hot paths dispatch across available Rust and polyglot backends over a pure-Python reference floor, with parity and benchmark provenance kept explicit.
The federated Studio surface exposes evaluate, prove, cosimulate, and benchmark verbs with recompute-verifiable evidence sealing and fail-closed claim boundaries.
Timing evidence distinguishes proved clock-cycle relations from still-gated named-device nanosecond closure and calibrated end-to-end sensor/driver/chamber measurements.
